searchDocs.title: conflictNext​
searchDocs.content: </> InMemoryStore.conflictNext( self: InMemoryStore, operation: string, count: number?, mutator: ((any) → any)?-- Receives the current value and returns the competing writer's value. Omit to re-run against unchanged state. ) → () Makes the next count updates lose a compare-and-set race. The transform runs once against the value it read, that result is discarded,mutator installs a competing write, and the transform runs again against the new value, which is what UpdateAsync does under contention. This is what catches a transform that fails to reset its own bookkeeping when re-entered, which every conditional write in Muster depends on.

searchDocs.title: legacyMaps​
searchDocs.content: </> Lanes.legacyMaps( settings: any, partition: string, count: number, lane: number, previous: number? ) → {string} The maps from previous that may hold tickets belonging to lane at count. A worker reads these alongside its own lane while the old count drains. Both counts are powers of two, since LaneScaler only doubles or halves from one, which makes this exact. A ticket hashes to h % count: Growing (count > previous): a ticket in old map o satisfies h % previous == o, so its new lane is one of o, o + previous, o + 2*previous, and so on. Reading old map lane % previous covers it. Shrinking (count < previous): h % count == (h % previous) % count, so every old map o with o % count == lane contributes. Either way the result holds at most previous / count entries: one when growing, two on a single halving.

searchDocs.title: sortedRange​
searchDocs.content: </> MemoryStore.sortedRange( self: MemoryStore, name: string, count: number, priority: number? ) → ( boolean, any ) Reads the oldest count entries. Sort keys are queue timestamps, so ascending order is first-come-first-served. NOTE MemoryStore caps a range read at 200 items. searchDocs.title: spreadScore​
searchDocs.content: </> Matcher.spreadScore( candidates: {Candidate}, indexes: {number} ) → ( number, number ) The default scoring function: rating spread across individual members, then total queue time. Both are minimised, compared in that order. Spread is measured per member rather than per ticket, so a group with a wide internal skill gap is penalised accordingly. Returns a spread of 0 when no candidate carries a rating, leaving queue time as the whole ordering, which is the behaviour an unrated queue wants.

Invites a player to the caller's party. The invite is written to an inbox keyed by the target's userId, so they can read it from whichever server they are on. searchDocs.content: On this page Runtime This item is only intended to be used by the module's authors. Private Show Private The only module in Muster that touches a Roblox global. Everything else receives what it needs through configuration, which is what lets the whole engine run headlessly under Lune against fakes. Each global is read through an any-typed local so the same source typechecks under Roblox (where game exists) and runs under Lune (where it resolves to nil).

searchDocs.title: enqueueGroup​
searchDocs.content: </> Matchmaker.enqueueGroup( self: any, userIds: {number}, options: GroupOptions? ) → Result<Ticket> Queues a set of players as one ticket. The group is never split across matches and is matched at its aggregate rating. Takes userIds directly and does not involve Party. The first userId becomes the ticket's leader, and is the only one who may cancel or acknowledge it. queue:enqueueGroup({ leaderId, friendId }, { ratings = ratings }) Groups larger than size.max are rejected with InvalidPartySize, and a repeated userId with DuplicateMember.

Only the party's leader may call this. The party's membership is locked for the lifetime of the ticket: invites, kicks, leaves, leadership transfers and disbanding all return PartyLocked until the ticket matches, is cancelled, or expires.

searchDocs.title: acknowledge​
searchDocs.content: </> Matchmaker.acknowledge( self: any, requesterUserId: number, ticketId: string ) → Result<MatchEnvelope<T>> Releases a matched ticket's players so they may queue again, and unlocks its party. This happens automatically on delivery unless manualAcknowledge is set. Enable that setting to hold the reservation until you have confirmed whatever follows the match, such as a teleport. A failure then leaves the players free to re-queue rather than locked out until their reservation expires.

searchDocs.content: </> Matchmaker.step(self: any) → () Runs one worker pass: ticket upkeep, lane acquisition, then a scan of each held lane. The worker thread calls this on a loop. Calling it directly advances the system one step, which is how the test suite drives it without yielding.

searchDocs.title: start​
searchDocs.content: </> Matchmaker.start(self: any) → () Starts the worker thread and subscribes for cross-server delivery. Called by the constructor unless autoStart is disabled. Calling it twice does nothing.

searchDocs.title: stop​
searchDocs.content: </> Matchmaker.stop(self: any) → () Stops the worker and releases every lane lease this server holds, so another server can take them immediately instead of waiting out the 15-second timeout. Suitable for game:BindToClose.

searchDocs.title: destroy​
searchDocs.content: </> Matchmaker.destroy(self: any) → () Calls Matchmaker:stop, disconnects the PlayerRemoving connection, and drops every signal handler.

searchDocs.title: health​
searchDocs.content: </> Matchmaker.health(self: any) → any A snapshot of this server's view of the queue, for logging or a debug command. Field Meaning localTickets Tickets this server enqueued and is still tracking. ownedLanes Lane leases this server currently holds. laneMode "auto" or "fixed". laneCount Lanes the default partition is sharded into. laneChanges Resizes this server has applied. throttled True once 1% of requests have come back throttled. broadcastHealthy False while message delivery looks unreliable. broadcastsSent / broadcastsReceived Message counts since start. requests Per-structure successes, failures, throttles and mean latency. Values are local to this server, not fleet-wide.

searchDocs.title: Metadata​
searchDocs.content: </> type Metadata = {[string]: any} Caller-supplied data carried on a ticket. Must survive a JSON round trip through MemoryStore: strings, numbers, booleans, and tables of those. Functions, Instances, cycles, and tables mixing array and dictionary keys are rejected at enqueue withInvalidMetadata. Limited to maxMetadataBytes (1024).

searchDocs.title: Member​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Member { userId: number serverId: string-- JobId of the server that enqueued them; where their match is delivered. rating: number?-- Present if and only if the queue is rated. provisional: boolean?-- True when rating.default was substituted for a missing rating. metadata: Metadata? } One player within a ticket or a match. serverId is per-member rather than per-ticket because a party's members can be on different servers, and each is notified on their own.

searchDocs.title: Ticket​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Ticket { id: string queue: string partition: string partyId: string? leaderUserId: number members: {Member} size: number rating: number?-- Party-aggregated rating, absent on unrated queues. metadata: Metadata? queuedAt: number expiresAt: number state: "Queued" | "Claimed" | "Matched" | "Cancelled" matchId: string? lane: number-- Index within the partition. laneCount: number-- Lane count in force when the ticket was written; lanes scale at runtime. } A queue entry covering one player or one group. A ticket is never split across matches.

searchDocs.title: MatchEnvelope​
searchDocs.content: </> interface MatchEnvelope { v: number-- Schema version. matchId: string queue: string partition: string createdAt: number size: number-- Total players across all members. members: {Member} ticketIds: {string} partyIds: {string} data: T-- The finalize hook's return value, or an empty table if there is no hook. } A committed match, delivered to every server holding one of its members. Generic over the finalizer's return type, so match.data.accessCode is typed and autocompletes. Deduplicate on matchId. The same set of players may appear under a second matchId if a worker stalled and its work was repaired.

searchDocs.title: MatchContext​
searchDocs.content: </> interface MatchContext { matchId: string queue: string partition: string members: {Member} ticketIds: {string} partyIds: {string} size: number averageRating: number?-- Mean member rating, absent on unrated queues. createdAt: number deadline: number-- Monotonic time the hook must return by. } The argument to a finalize hook: everything known about the match before the hook's own return value is attached.

searchDocs.title: AbortReason​
searchDocs.content: </> type AbortReason = "FinalizerError" | "FinalizerTimeout" | "FinalizerTooLarge" | "LeaseLost" | "StoreUnavailable" | "TicketStolen" Why a match that had already claimed its tickets failed to commit. Its players return to the queue in every case. Reason Cause FinalizerError The hook threw. FinalizerTimeout The hook did not return within finalizeTimeout. FinalizerTooLarge The hook's return value failed validation or exceeded maxMatchDataBytes. LeaseLost Another server took the lane while the hook was yielding. StoreUnavailable MemoryStore rejected the commit. TicketStolen A ticket was claimed by another match between selection and commit.

searchDocs.title: AbortContext​
searchDocs.content: </> interface AbortContext { matchId: string queue: string partition: string members: {Member} reason: AbortReason message: string?-- The hook's error text, when reason is FinalizerError. data: any?-- The hook's return value, if it produced one before the abort. } The argument to onAbort. When data is present, the hook ran to completion and its side effects outlived a match that never formed.

searchDocs.title: Finalizer​
searchDocs.content: </> type Finalizer = (context: MatchContext) → T Runs once per matchId, on the server that formed the match, after its tickets are claimed and before it commits. Expected to yield. The same set of players may be finalized again under a different matchId if this match aborts, so deduplicate on matchId.

searchDocs.title: AbortHandler​
searchDocs.content: </> type AbortHandler = (context: AbortContext) → ()

searchDocs.title: QueueStatus​
searchDocs.content: </> type QueueStatus = { state: "Queued", queuedAt: number } | {state: "Claiming"} | { state: "Matched", match: MatchEnvelope<T> } | {state: "Cancelled"} | {state: "Expired"}

searchDocs.title: ErrorCode​
searchDocs.content: </> type ErrorCode = string The codes a ServiceError can carry. Switch on this rather than on the message text, which is not stable.

searchDocs.title: ServiceError​
searchDocs.content: </> interface ServiceError { code: ErrorCode message: string retryable: boolean-- True when the same call may succeed on a later attempt. }

searchDocs.title: Result​
searchDocs.content: </> type Result = { ok: true, value: T } | { ok: false, error: ServiceError } Returned by every method that touches the network. Invalid configuration and invalid arguments throw instead. See Result.

searchDocs.title: SortedItem​
searchDocs.content: </> interface SortedItem { key: string value: any sortKey: number }

searchDocs.title: Store​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Store {} The storage contract, implemented by Muster.stores.MemoryStore against Roblox MemoryStore and by Muster.stores.InMemory against tables. Every method returns (success, value) and must not throw. update must be a compare-and-set: the transform may be invoked more than once for a single call, and returning nil from it must abort the write.

searchDocs.title: Subscription​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Subscription { disconnect: (self: any) → () }

searchDocs.title: Messaging​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Messaging {} The notification contract. Delivery is assumed to be best-effort and unordered; Muster never depends on a message arriving.

searchDocs.title: Candidate​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Candidate { ticketId: string partyId: string? size: number rating: number? ratings: {number} queuedAt: number } The reduced view of a ticket held in the lane index and passed to Matcher. Kept small because it is read far more often than the ticket record itself.

searchDocs.title: MatcherPolicy​
searchDocs.content: </> interface MatcherPolicy { minSize: number targetSize: number maxSize: number fallbackAfter: number-- Seconds before a below-target group is accepted. compatible: ( anchor: Candidate, candidate: Candidate, waitSeconds: number ) → boolean score: ( candidates: {Candidate}, indexes: {number} ) → ( number, number ) } Everything Matcher knows about how to group candidates. Supply one through the matcher config field to replace the rating window with role composition, region affinity, or any other rule. compatible decides whether a candidate may join an anchor's group. score returns (primary, secondary), both minimized and compared in that order. The built-in policy uses rating spread, then total queue time.

searchDocs.title: RatingConfig​
searchDocs.content: </> interface RatingConfig { window: number?-- Starting rating tolerance. Default 200. relax: number?-- Extra tolerance per second waited. Default 40. maxWindow: number?-- Ceiling on the widened window. Default infinite. unbounded: number?-- Seconds after which any rating matches. Default 60. default: number?-- Substituted when a caller omits a rating. Default nil, which makes omission an error. aggregate: (({number}) → number)?-- Party rating from member ratings. Default is a max-biased mean. } Supplying this table makes a queue rated. Omit it for an unrated queue, where tickets carry no rating and matching is oldest-first. Rated and unrated is a per-queue property: a rated queue requires a rating for every player, and an unrated one rejects them.

searchDocs.title: SizeConfig​
searchDocs.content: </> interface SizeConfig { min: number target: number? max: number? } Match sizing. size = 6 is shorthand for all three being 6, and target defaults to max. A group reaching target commits immediately. A smaller one waits fallbackAfter seconds, after which the largest group down to min is accepted.

searchDocs.title: EnqueueOptions​
searchDocs.content: </> interface EnqueueOptions { rating: number?-- Required on a rated queue unless rating.default is set. Throws on an unrated queue. metadata: Metadata? partition: string?-- Overrides partitionKey for this ticket. Partitions never match each other. serverId: string?-- Overrides where this member's match is delivered. Defaults to this server. }

searchDocs.title: GroupOptions​
searchDocs.content: </> interface GroupOptions { ratings: {[number]: number}?-- Per-userId ratings, required on a rated queue without a default. metadata: Metadata? partition: string?-- Overrides partitionKey for this ticket. serverIds: {[number]: string}?-- Per-userId delivery addresses, for members on other servers. }

searchDocs.title: PartyMember​
searchDocs.content: </> interface PartyMember { userId: number joinedAt: number serverId: string? }

searchDocs.title: PartyQueue​
searchDocs.content: </> interface PartyQueue { ticketId: string state: "Queued" | "Matched" matchId: string? expiresAt: number }

searchDocs.title: PartyView​
searchDocs.content: </> interface PartyView { id: string leaderUserId: number members: {PartyMember} createdAt: number version: number-- Incremented on every mutation; compare it to detect a stale read. queue: PartyQueue?-- Non-nil while queued, during which membership is frozen. }

searchDocs.title: PartyInvite​
searchDocs.content: </> interface PartyInvite { id: string partyId: string leaderUserId: number targetUserId: number createdAt: number expiresAt: number }

searchDocs.content: </> type Logger = ( level: "info" | "warn" | "error", message: string, fields: {[string]: any} ) → ()

searchDocs.content: </> type Metrics = ( name: string, value: number, tags: {[string]: any} ) → ()
